name: Routine Argument Writing
description: Routine Argument Writing helps us nurture community and civil discourse in our classrooms. Regular low-stakes, high-impact writing invitations can support young writers as they build the skills needed to grapple with some of the complexities of advanced argument writing, such as debate, controversial issues, and researching opposing points of view. Equally important, these routine practices foster student agency when we invite them to engage in conversations about arguments in their lives.
criteria: Earn all Exploring Argument in our Lives, Arguments in Response to Single Texts, Arguments in Response to Multiple Texts, and Writing and Revising Claims micro credentials.

Routine Argument Writing

National Writing Project

Description

Routine Argument Writing helps us nurture community and civil discourse in our classrooms. Regular low-stakes, high-impact writing invitations can support young writers as they build the skills needed to grapple with some of the complexities of advanced argument writing, such as debate, controversial issues, and researching opposing points of view. Equally important, these routine practices foster student agency when we invite them to engage in conversations about arguments in their lives.

Criteria

Earn all Exploring Argument in our Lives, Arguments in Response to Single Texts, Arguments in Response to Multiple Texts, and Writing and Revising Claims micro credentials.
